title: The Four Heavenly Kings
paragraphs: "This is dangerous! The Demon King is going to take over the world!"
"I'm not interested. Gaelion may look down on people sometimes, but he’s not despairing.”

Damn it! Rival isn’t even looking at me! Aren’t you just a figurehead dragon, a mere decoration? When on earth did you acquire such skills? In the previous loop, you were just playing around saying “na na na”!
“Hmm… So you were someone like the Queen of Melromarc or Princess Melty. It feels like night and day compared to when you’re out hunting with Lord Iwatani.”
“I’m just drawing on the Dragon Emperor’s experiences—it’s not all Gaelion’s own experience, you know.”
“That may be true, but I still think it’s pretty impressive.”

“Thank you. Besides, these are the subordinates I gained as a result of being thanked for wiping out the griffins—the ones whose numbers had grown so large within the kingdom that they were causing trouble for the people and running amok as if the place belonged to them.”

Griffins… Come to think of it, they were under Takt’s command. That means those guys were getting preferential treatment for their own species, didn’t they? They’re a bunch who’re way too lenient with their own kind.
“Was there a problem like that?”

“Yes… It’s thought that Takt was involved in that sort of thing. There were definitely some among them who said things that pointed to it when we took them down, so there’s no doubt about it. Even though Takt is gone, they just won’t give up.”
“Come to think of it, Griffin was one of Takt’s crew, wasn’t he?”
“I heard the previous king was also killed a long time ago while inspecting the various nations. They say the princess was killed by the Spear Hero.”
Since this was my doing, I gave Father a thumbs-up while flashing him a bright smile. Father reacted as if he were used to this.
“...I seem to recall hearing something like that, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Did I?”
“Yeah. When you took down the Griffin in Takt, Motoyasu-kun, you said something like, ‘I’ll send it to the same place as its parent.’”
“Did I? Oh, was that during this loop? That’s the original Griffin Edge I gave to Éclair.”
Since I’ve been looping through all sorts of things, there’s a lot I’ve forgotten. There have been so many loops where I’ve taken down Griffins that I’d completely forgotten.
“Hey! What kind of junk are you handing me?!”
Éclair protested. Is there a problem? I was just lending you a handy tool.
“I’d really rather not be the target here. Could you step back a bit?”
“Lord Rasa, that’s not funny at all, even as a joke!”
“It’ll be fine, won’t it? I’m not taking any responsibility, though.”
“Seriously…”
“It’s just a griffin, after all. As long as Filolial-sama is here, that’s plenty.”
“After all, they’re just griffins. As long as we have a dragon, that’s enough.”
……Rival and I said that almost at the same time. Why do I have to be in sync with you of all people!?
“You two just look like two peas in a pod… I guess you really do start to resemble each other when you loop?”
“That’s hurtful.”
“It is hurtful. I just taught those cocky guys a lesson and made them behave. This alone has improved life in Shieldfreeden, even if only slightly.”
“Hmm… I hope this doesn’t turn into an unnecessary commotion… Or rather, do the monsters know where the remaining Takt members are?”
“It seems ties with the Griffin faction have already been severed. I don’t know when we’ll be able to get in touch.”
“I see…”
“Boo.”

By the way, Filolial-sama and the others are traveling with us as well. Sakura-chan has been particularly grumpy lately. Even so, she seems to be enjoying herself while she’s with Father. Ugh… Sakura-chan is truly a sweet little thing.
“What’s wrong, Sakura-chan?”
“Gaelion said the other day that if Naofumi acts as his bodyguard, he’ll appoint him to the Four Heavenly Kings.”
Hey, what’s going on here?! This is the first I’ve heard of that!
“That’s right. Since Gaelion is entrusting Naofumi to me, I thought I’d appoint Sakura-chan as the Wind Four Heavenly King. I’ll bestow a little blessing upon her—with salt.”
“What are you planning to do to Sakura-chan?! Depending on your answer, I’ll kill you!”
“I’m just going to use technology from another world to give her a power-up that won’t conflict with her Filolial powers. It’s ‘Power-Up Sakura’—even the Spear Hero will be happy.”
“Don’t go doing something like that on your own!”
How dare you do such a thing! How do you plan to take responsibility if Sakura-chan catches some weird disease!
“If she adapts well, we might even be able to change her hair color to gold and her eye color to blue. The Spear Hero wanted her to be like that, didn’t he?”
“Ugh…”
Are you trying to make Sakura-chan more like Filo-tan through external factors!? Rival! What’s your objective here!? You’re fundamentally wrong to begin with.
“Sakura-chan is… Sakura-chan, after all!”
“The Spear Hero has a pretty troublesome personality, too…”
“Even so, she’s a good person at heart.”
“Of course. I’d be disappointed if anyone here actually agreed with that.”
What’s so disappointing about that? Disappointment is a trait unique to you dragons.
“Since there’s no helping it, I’ll just leave the blessing inactive for now.”
“Wait a minute! Have you already cast it!?”
“I’m just planting the seed while I’m setting up the Magic spell.”
“I’ll definitely kill you!”
“Um… it’s kind of scary to think that with Gaelion-chan around, that girl Filo might actually pull it off.”
“It could turn into an experiment, so I won’t do it without your approval.”
That goes without saying. You can’t trust dragons, after all.
“Um…”
At that point, the council member who had been pushing for the dragon initiative furrowed his brow deeply as he showed the documents to Rival.
“Sigh…”
Rival looked at the documents, sighed, and took a sip of the tea that had been served.
“What? Is something wrong?”

“No, I’m coming to the assembly, but a faction that refuses to recognize Gaelion and the others as new dragons has thrown a tough problem my way. I just looked at the progress report, saw the result I expected, and I’m just dumbfounded.”
“What kind of difficult issue is that?”
“It’s a problem in a poverty-stricken area within Shieldfreeden. This issue has been going on since way back, around the time Shieldfreeden was founded… It’s quite a complicated matter.”
“When you say a difficult issue in Shieldfreeden, you mean that one, don’t you…”
Panda furrows his brow as if he has an idea, muttering to himself. If even Lars-chan knows about it, does that mean it’s that well-known?
“Do you know about it too, Lars-chan? Is it really that famous?”
“Well, in Zeltoble, there are merchants who make a business out of that sort of thing. I’m sure even in Melromarc, the more lighthearted topics make their way around from time to time, don’t they?”
Panda glances at Éclair and tilts his head suggestively. Too bad! Éclair’s political acumen is pretty low! It’s a waste of time to expect anything from him.
“Hm?”
“The way I see it, you can’t pour water in until you plug the hole in the bottom. But even with those plant seeds, you still couldn’t do it?”
“If I could, I wouldn’t be here.”
“I see. Well, there’s nothing we can do about it, I guess…”
It seems Rival and the panda are utterly exasperated.
“Hey, what’s this all about? Won’t you tell me?”
“Well then, let’s go over the facts… Even before the waves caused famines and droughts, there were already regions and countries suffering from famine.”
“Yeah. If we can operate this bio-plant correctly, there’s a good chance we can solve the famine problem, right? We figured that out after talking to people in both Siltvelt and Melromarc.”

Father replied, looking as if he had an idea what I was getting at. That’s right. In this world, there are places where the seasons and weather have been thrown into chaos by the waves, leading to frequent disasters like famines and droughts. But that’s just a matter of holding out until we overcome the final wave. Above all, it’s a problem that can be easily resolved by using the bio-plant to produce food.
Unfortunately, Rivals snatched the fame away from me, but I did receive words of praise from Father. What a blessing!

“But you know… in countries where politics are corrupt, the higher-ups are thoroughly rotten. They collect taxes even when people can’t even afford tomorrow’s meal, and then call on other nations to provide food. They act all civilized even though they’re poor.”
“In a world like this, isn’t that basically like asking to be invaded?”
“It makes for an easy excuse to invade, too. ‘We’re at war because we have no food,’ they say.”
“Hmm…”

“Peace—that concept spread by the heroes of the past—is just that hard to maintain. And it was Shieldfreeden, a fairly powerful nation, that was providing aid to regions within its own borders struggling with poverty. They were making all sorts of appeals. ‘Let’s save those starving in poverty all over the world.’”
It sounds like a good story at first glance, but there’s something unsettling about it. I seem to recall hearing a similar story in Japan, too.
“Isn’t that a good thing? Foreign countries—and major powers, no less—are acting out of goodwill.”

“To a certain extent, yes. Things like improving roads or creating environments where people can learn—wherever improvements can be made, they’re made. But there are some people in this world who are just beyond help. The local nobility usually pockets a portion of the supplies sent to them before distributing the rest.”
“Ugh…”
Father looks absolutely appalled. It’s certainly a terrible story—enough to make anyone recoil. Rival lets out a sigh right here.
“By the way, I recall that even after removing those nobles from office, stripping them of their privileges, and shifting the focus to reconstruction, it still didn’t work.”
“Oh? Have they already tried that?”

“I just remember hearing about that sort of problem in the world of *Wild Ofumi*, which has since become peaceful. To elaborate, after that noble pockets a portion, the next transport convoy pockets more, and then the guys who’ve staked a claim to the road take a cut as a toll—and this kind of back-and-forth keeps happening until the goods reach their destination.”
“……Wait a minute. How much is left by the time they actually reach their destination?”
Rival, Panda, and the Dragon Advocacy Representative all quickly looked away. It seems things have gotten pretty dire.
“Isn’t that putting the cart before the horse…? Then wouldn’t it be better for Gaelion-chan to go out there herself and distribute the food?”
“We did try that, but wasn’t it confiscated later?”

“Yes… In that region, along with the outdated belief that ‘face’ is everything, there’s a tendency to view any behavior that deviates from that belief with extreme hostility… Moreover, dangerous technologies like poisons and drugs have developed to a surprisingly advanced level.”

While places like Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden are all about brute force, in that region, face—or pride—is what matters most. If their face is lost, they’ll likely plot an assassination using underhanded schemes. Those kinds of people would probably mobilize the entire settlement to come and lynch us. I can tell those foolish lot think just like Takt—they’re all cut from the same cloth. HAHAHA, we’ll turn the tables on them!
“Oh, I see… Well then, all the more reason to make them plant and tend to the bio-plants, don’t you think?”
“If Gaelion’s memory serves me right, the day after they were planted, they were cut down, turned into firewood, and sold at the nearby market.”
“Yes. You understand perfectly…”

That’s actually pretty impressive. To eradicate something so troublesome that even Father said it kept growing back no matter how many times you cut it down. It’s my fault—if I’d distributed them like I did to that village in the past, the Bio-Plants might not have run amok.
“If they’d just waited, everyone would have had enough to eat, but they prioritized short-term profits… It’s hopeless, isn’t it…”
“It’s too much of a challenge. I think it’s impossible, no matter how you look at it.”
“Of course. I’m pretty sure even that miser Takt left that area alone.”

So it’s that problem area where even Takt couldn’t find a way to make money? In a way, that’s impressive. It’s quite something that the Takt faction—which used “corporate slave drinks” to keep people in line and secretly eliminated anyone who disobeyed orders—wouldn’t touch it.

“According to Nelshen’s activity logs, it seems he went there a few times, but all that happened was that the local leader was replaced. I suppose Takt couldn’t carry out a full-scale purge because of the public backlash. There’s no financial incentive there, after all.”

I heard that foreign countries and major powers are providing food aid there. If they were to destroy a place like that, condemnation from neighboring nations would be inevitable. So it’s a troublesome area, including land that’s of no use whatsoever.
“As for what ‘Wild Ofumi’ was worried about regarding this issue—it wasn’t just that.”
Oh? Was Father worried about that in the first world? I can’t imagine Father, who makes decisions without hesitation, having that kind of weakness.
“Is there some other reason?”
“Was there something like that?”
“I’m not sure I agree with that ‘nothing matters except Filolial, the Spear Hero’ mentality… Don’t you remember that was one of the reasons your Filo went on tour to Shieldfreeden?”
“That’s not true at all! As far as I remember, Filo-chan’s live tour was a resounding success!”
The glorious image of Filo-chan still remains vivid in my mind. It’s the sight of Filo-chan, sparkling on stage, dancing and singing so adorably. Shieldfreeden? I couldn’t care less about that.
“Of course I was only watching Filo.”
“Well…”
“Yeah.”
“Hmm, no doubt about it. That’s exactly what I’d expect from Lord Kitamura.”
“I don’t quite follow the conversation, but I understand that part regarding the Spear Hero.”
Father—who looks a bit awkward—and the other two knights are all in agreement. I can’t quite wrap my head around Éclair’s look of understanding. I don’t need that kind of trust.
That’s not it at all! I’m just completely devoted to Filo-chan!
